To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ca2+ channel activity of the cerebellar type I inositol 3,4,5 trisphosphate receptor is not regulated by the cytoplasm Ca2+ concentration in a bell-shaped manner and that the Ca2+-independent inactivation is mediated by calmodin.
the Ca2+-dependence of the cerebellar type I IP3R/Ca2+ channel is not an intrinsic characteristic of the channel protein, and the Ca-dependent inactivation of the channel is mediated by calmodulins.
the Ca2+-inhibition is a property of the native IP3R1 in cerebellar membranes, and the inhibition is mediated by calmoduline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the Ca2+-mediated regulation of inositol trisphosphate receptor function in the cerebellum.
the molecular mechanisms of the Ca2+-induced inactivation of the cerebellar type-1 IP3R.
the role of calmodulin in the regulation of the cerebellar IP3R1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IP3R does not have a bell-shaped Ca2+ dependence and that the Ca2+-dependence of the IP3Rs is mediated by calmodulins.
Ca2+-dependent regulation of the IP3 receptor is a result of Ca2+/calmodulin-mediated inactivation.

the bell-shaped Ca(2+) dependency is not an intrinsic function of the IP3 receptor, but that it is due to the presence of Ca(2+) binding proteins, which bind Ca(2+) and modulate the function of the IP(3) receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the IP3Rs are Ca2+ sensors, but the bell-shaped dependence of the IP3Rs is not an intrinsic Ca2+ sensing property of the IP(3)Rs but is due to Ca2+-dependent modulation by calmodulin, which is a Ca2+ sensor.
the IP3Rs have two Ca2+-dependent regulatory mechanisms, Ca2+-dependent inhibition and Ca2+-dependent activation.
the IP3R is a Ca2+ channel that is not regulated by Ca2+, but rather by calmodulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calmodulin, which is present in all eukaryotes, is a general regulator of IP3Rs and that the Ca2+ sensitivity and Ca2+-dependent modulation of IP3Rs are regulated by calmodulin.
the Ca2+-independent activation of IP3 receptors by calmodulin is a general phenomenon, and it is a mechanism that allows IP3 receptors to respond to Ca2+ signals in the physiological range.
the Ca2+ binding sites of the IP3 receptor that regulate the gating of the channel are not the same as those that regulate the Ca2+-sensitivity of IP3 binding.
